content:
mara: quick heads-up — ran a focused smoke run on the new kernel handoff with interleaved KV layout + FlashAttention2 fallback. seeing weird p50/p99 divergence on short sequences (<=64). attaching minimal repro and profiler snippets.

devin: thanks, can you paste the small repro?

mara: pasted below — workload = chat-like, batch=16, seqs random 8-64, dtype=bfloat16, kernel selection rule = prefer fused when batch>8 otherwise flash.

mara: repro command:
```bash
./run_infer --model llama2-13b --batch 16 --seq_min 8 --seq_max 64 --kv-layout interleaved --kernels policy.json --dtype bf16
```

sanjay: what are the exact numbers?

mara: profiler top lines:
```
kernel_select: FlashAttention2 chosen 72% of calls
fallback to FusedAttn: 28% (usually seq<=16)
per-token throughput: mean 12.4k tok/s, p50 latency 18ms, p99 latency 142ms
with separate-KV layout (same run but switched) p99 98ms
```

alyssa: interesting — that's a big p99 gap. could be bank conflicts in interleaved layout when small seqs trigger different kernel path. did you capture smem / sdram stalls in nvprof?

mara: nvprof snapshot: SMEM_STALL 21%, MEM_BW_UTIL 65%, warp_serialize 3%. For separate-KV run SMEM_STALL 9% and MEM_BW_UTIL 82%.

devin: so separate-KV uses more bandwidth but less shared memory contention. that fits bank conflict hypothesis. do we have stride alignment bytes?

mara: interleaved layout uses 64-byte stride per head (packed), headers aligned to 128. but when seq small, the fused kernel packs kv differently and ends up with odd 32-byte offsets for some banks.

sanjay: can you try forcing the kernel selector to always pick fused and compare? if fused wins, likely a kernel mismatch with interleaved layout for small seq.

mara: forced fused only: p99 = 110ms (better than mixed but worse than separate-KV). forcing Flash only: p99 = 156ms. so mixed switching seems particularly bad due to fallback overhead + cache layout mismatch.

alyssa: fallback overhead + KV format conversion cost could explain it. Do we convert interleaved -> fused internal layout at runtime?

mara: yes, we do an on-the-fly remap when switching kernels. cost ~= 0.8ms per request in this workload, which multiplies over tokens for short sequences because we lose batching benefits.

perf-bot: perf-regression-detection: alert triggered (p99 increased 45% vs baseline separate-KV). ticket created: #INF-5342

devin: ideas: 1) prefer stable kernel per connection (sticky routing) to avoid remap churn; 2) add a cheap remap cache keyed by (batch, seq, layout); 3) tweak selector to avoid Flash on seq<=16 with interleaved layout.

alyssa: also consider aligning interleaved stride to 128 bytes (pad) to reduce bank conflict. that will increase memory but may reduce SMEM stalls. need memory tradeoff analysis.

mara: quick micro-bench: padding to 128b reduced SMEM_STALL to 11% and p99 down to 102ms (still not as good as separate-KV 98ms).

sanjay: worth trying sticky kernel + pad together. sticky should avoid conversion ramp cost. can you run combined?

mara: combined sticky+kpad run: p99 93ms, p50 17ms, throughput slightly better. looks promising.

devin: nice — if sticky reduces remap churn, selector can be updated to sticky by default for dedicated pools. For hosted API we can expose as a knob.

ops-bot: deploy canary: eng-runtime/fallback-fix v0.3.2 -> 3% of traffic, scheduled 2024-11-12T09:30:00Z

alyssa: can we add unit/perf test that simulates high rate of short seq churn to avoid regressions? add to the CI perf harness.

mara: open PR with test + selector change in draft: https://repo/rw/inference/pulls/2123 — needs review.

devin: assign to sanjay for kernel selector logic review, alyssa for perf harness and memory tradeoffs.

sanjay: taking it. will also check INT8 path because quantization changes packing and might hit same issue.

mara: FYI, INT8 interleaved run had even higher SMEM stalls (29%) and p99 180ms. add to PR notes.

devin: good capture. thanks mara. we'll triage and follow up in the ticket. :thumbsup:

mara: thanks — I'll attach the full perf trace to INF-5342 and update the PR with sticky option default for dedicated pools.
